_about: Routing data for ai-animation-routing. Read by cli/aar.py and by the knowledge docs. Model names, capabilities and prices ROT — the 2026-08-15 version of this file was already wrong by 2026-08-17 (veo3 had been removed; veo3.1 had GAINED keyframe-pair support). Run `aar probe` to re-derive from the live API before trusting any row.
_verified_how: Live probe of POST /image_to_video. Capability flags come from the API's own validation errors; costs marked `estimated` come from the estimatedCost the API returns on task creation, with every probe task cancelled immediately (cancelling straight away was observed to cost nothing). Costs marked `observed` were measured across a real production build.
_units: cost_credits are Runway API credits; ~$0.01/credit at 10,000 credits for ~$100.

runway.note: Acts as a multi-vendor gateway. Billed separately from the runwayml.com app subscription.

capabilities._note: keyframe_pair = accepts a promptImage ARRAY with position first/last. Verified 2026-08-17 by probe.

eager_image_validation._note: These reject a bad image at submit time — a probe against them creates no task. The others validate lazily and WILL create a task from a probe payload; cancel it immediately.

notes: First choice for anything with a defined start and end state, and the cheapest of the 1080p keyframe-pair models by a wide margin.
Lowest measured frame-to-frame jitter of the models tested on near-still shots (0.010-0.026 vs 0.063 for seedance2) — a dated measurement on one subject, not a law. Measure your own with `aar qc`.
Strong keyframe adherence: honours both supplied endpoints rather than drifting toward its own idea of the shot.
Returns 1924x1076 rather than exactly 1920x1080, and carries a silent AAC audio track. Conform and strip audio at delivery — `aar` does this automatically.
Validates image dimensions at submit time, so a bad input costs nothing.
Strictest moderation classifier of the set on human-subject framing. If it blocks, change the framing or switch vendor — do not resubmit unchanged.
The escape hatch. Different vendor, different moderation classifier — cleared every shot the Kling family refused, usually on the first attempt.

Goes to 4K NATIVELY (3840:2160 and beyond). If you need above 1080p, generating here beats generating at 1080p and running a creative upscaler — no invented detail, no temporal-irregularity risk. Worth the premium over kling3.0_pro for that case specifically.
Roughly 2.4x the cost of kling3.0_pro for the same 5s 1080p shot. Reach for it when you need it, not by default.
Visibly stuttery on near-still shots relative to kling3.0_pro. Prefer it for motion, not for locked plates.
Validates lazily: a malformed submission still creates a billable task. Check your submissions.
Carries an audio track. Strip on conform.
CAPABILITY CHANGED: as of 2026-08-17 this DOES accept a keyframe pair. It did not in early August. This is the clearest example in the repo of why you probe before trusting a table.
Duration is constrained — 5s submissions were rejected where 8s was accepted. Check before batching.
Historically the model that rarely moderation-blocks, which makes it useful when a subject is refused elsewhere.

Historically re-stages static compositions on longer single-image takes (rotating subjects, recentring, resizing props). That observation predates keyframe-pair support and may not hold when both ends are pinned — verify on your own shot before trusting it for locked composition.
Expensive: ~320 credits for 8s at 720p, against ~85 for 5s at 1080p on kling3.0_pro.
Cheaper veo3.1 tier — 120 credits against 320 for the same 8s 720p shot. Same duration constraints. Quality untested here.
Newer seedance tier, and the most expensive keyframe-pair option measured — 4x kling3.0_pro for the same shot. Quality untested here; do not reach for it on price.
Cheaper seedance tier at 720p. Quality untested here.
Cheapest keyframe-pair option measured. Useful for testing whether a keyframe pair works at all before committing to a good model. Quality untested here.
Accepts keyframe pairs. Another vendor, so another moderation classifier — a second escape hatch if seedance also refuses your subject.
Duration constrained: 5s submissions rejected. Untested for quality.
Same vendor as kling3.0_pro, so a moderation block on one is likely to repeat here — switch VENDOR rather than working down this list for filter reasons.
Older Kling tier, still accepts keyframe pairs.
Cheaper Kling tier.

4K Kling tier, accepts keyframe pairs. Untested here — but note that generating at your delivery resolution beats generating small and upscaling, so this is worth evaluating before you plan an upscale pass.
CANNOT take a keyframe pair — the API rejects the array outright: 'Too big: expected array to have <=1 items'.
SILENTLY CAPS AT 720p — the allowed-ratio list has no 1080p option. Building a pipeline on it forces an upscale pass that a 1080p-native model would have made unnecessary.
Observed drifting colour temperature and framing across a take (24% cooling, 15px centroid travel) in ways invisible in a 3-frame check and obvious in measurement. `aar qc` reports both.
Single image only. Superseded by gen4.5.
Single image only.
No longer in the API's model enum as of 2026-08-17. It was a documented workhorse two weeks earlier. Kept here as a tombstone: pin nothing to a model name without a probe.
Obeys REMOVE-object and ADD-object instructions well and preserves everything else. The right tool when you like a clip and need one thing gone.
IGNORES 're-render this region in a different style' instructions. Two full passes produced measurable no-ops. Do not use it for restyling.

Not surgical when the edit is entangled with an adjacent property. Asked to remove one feature from a subject, it also stripped a colour treatment the shot depended on. When the fix touches the subject's appearance, fix the SOURCE KEYFRAME and regenerate — cheaper and cleaner.
Works fine on rendered/generated footage. Moderation blocks observed only on real footage of identifiable people.
2x. Genuinely sharper. It is a CREATIVE upscaler — it invents plausible detail rather than interpolating.

Safe on CG and clean synthetic renders. BREAKS live-action with fine moving texture — hair, beard, knitwear — because it invents that detail slightly differently on every frame, doubling temporal irregularity into visible stutter. Completely invisible in still frames.
Never sign off an upscale on stills alone. `aar qc --compare` measures frame-to-frame irregularity against the source.
Better still: generate at delivery resolution and skip this entirely.
All stills and still edits. Accepts multiple reference images alongside the text prompt.
Edit-derive rather than regenerate: every variant should be an edit of an approved parent image, attached fresh each time. Regenerating from text alone re-rolls identity.
Attach only the references you want obeyed. A style anchor left in the stack alongside a newer canonical frame will fight it — observed snapping a subject back to the anchor's pose and camera.
Properties you do not mention still drift. Pin saturation and anything else you are relying on.
